source_text: Si enim qui sunt ex lege, haeredes sunt, evacuata est fides, destructa est repromissio [n220] . Qui sermo nisi intellegatur, ingerit maximam quaestionem; dubio enim procul dicit eos esse ex lege, quos supra dixerat ex circumcisione, quos sibi tantum noverat arrogare, ut putarent praeter se neminem assumi ad Abrahae seminis dignitatem; atque hoc disputatione collegerat, ut quia non solum hi, qui ex circumcisione, sed et illi, qui ex praeputio sectari voluissent vestigia fidei Abrahae, non immerito Abrahae filii censerentur.
pass_a_gloss: For if those who are from the law are heirs, faith has been emptied, the promise has been destroyed. Which speech unless it is understood thrusts in a very great question; for beyond doubt he says those are from the law whom he had said above from circumcision, whom he had known to arrogate so much to themselves that they thought besides themselves no one is taken up unto the dignity of Abraham's seed; and he had collected this by disputation, so that because not only these who from circumcision, but also those who from foreskin had wanted to follow the footprints of Abraham's faith, would not unmeritedly be estimated sons of Abraham.

lemmas.lexica: LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin

pass_b_english: ‘For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith is emptied and the promise destroyed’ (Romans 4:14). Unless this statement is understood, it introduces a very great difficulty. Undoubtedly by ‘those who are of the law’ he means those whom he had earlier called ‘of the circumcision.’ He knew they claimed so much for themselves that they thought no one besides themselves could be admitted to the dignity of Abraham’s offspring. Yet his argument had established that not only the circumcised, but also those of the uncircumcised who chose to follow the footsteps of Abraham’s faith, should rightly be reckoned Abraham’s children.
